text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Rights campaign group National Child Rights Project says it has sent a proposal on banning street trading by children to military ruler General Sani Abacha for approval.
- State-run power company National Electric Power Authority orders Nigerian Gas Company to delay the cleaning of pipelines carrying gas to power plants feeding the national grid.
- Four people and a circus monkey are injured when a device explodes in a Lagos surburb in one of of numerous bombing incidents since November in the Nigerian city.
- Capital market operators urge military government to introduce in the awaited 1997 fiscal budget privatisation and tax incentives to encourage foreign investments.
- Chief executive of state-owned Nigeria Fertiliser Co, Nathaniel Ejiga, is sacked for opposing removal of restrictions on the importation of some brands of fertilisers, sources say.
- The first batch of Christian pilgrims will leave for Jerusalem from the capital Abuja on Sunday aboard national carrier Nigerian Airways, spokesman Chris Aligbe says.
